units.title: OP Stack chains with ETH gas
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-873 and L-878. Finding F-138 (cycle 18, governance): Nitro builds an ArbitrumContractTx from a parent chain message with From set to the message's sender field, and runs it without a nonce check and without the check that the sender has no code. If a message could carry the PoolManager address as sender, a plain transfer call on a pooled token in the PoolManager's name would move its balance without unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 291-297). Cycle 18 cleared this for ordinary accounts because the stock Inbox passes every sender through applyL1ToL2Alias in _deliverToBridge, but that was read from the main branch of OffchainLabs/nitro-contracts, not from what is deployed. Task 1: for Arbitrum One (parent Ethereum), Robinhood Chain (chain 4663, parent Ethereum) and Elysium (chain 99901, parent HyperEVM, chain 999), find the Inbox, SequencerInbox, Bridge and Rollup addresses from the rollup's own records (research/network-risk/state and the cycles/016 and cycles/018 arbitrum-family work directories hold some; otherwise the chain's documentation and Bridge.allowedDelayedInboxList). Read the EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots of each Inbox and Bridge proxy with eth_getStorageAt, fetch the implementation bytecode with eth_getCode, and fetch verified source from Sourcify or the explorer where it exists. Task 2: from the deployed bytecode (selector table first, then the code behind each selector) list every externally callable function of each Inbox implementation and say, for each one that enqueues a message, how the sender field given to the Bridge is computed: aliased msg.sender, msg.sender unaliased under a condition (which condition), or a caller-chosen value. Cover sendUnsignedTransaction, sendContractTransaction, sendL1FundedUnsignedTransaction, sendL1FundedContractTransaction, the ToFork variants, sendL2Message, sendL2MessageFromOrigin, createRetryableTicket, unsafeCreateRetryableTicket, depositEth and any function that the main branch does not have. Say whether the Arbitrum One implementation after the Security Council action of 2026-10-30 is the one that was in place before it (compare code hashes over time with eth_getCode at old blocks, or the upgrade events). Task 3: list every address in each Bridge's allowed delayed inbox list and outbox list and decide for each whether it can enqueue a message with a sender it chooses. Task 4: the alias. A message from parent chain address A arrives with sender A + 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111. For each of the three chains compute the parent chain address that would alias to that chain's PoolManager, check with eth_getCode and eth_getTransactionCount on the parent chain that nothing is deployed there, and say what it would take for anyone to act from that address. Task 5, transfer to the OP Stack: for OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo and X Layer, say how a deposit transaction (type 0x7e) gets its from field (OptimismPortal depositTransaction aliases a contract caller and leaves an EOA caller as is), whether op-reth and op-geth run a deposit whose from has code without a nonce or code check, and read the deployed portal implementation of at least three of the chains from bytecode in the same way. An entry point that lets an account without a role put the PoolManager address, or any chosen address, into the sender field is a finding with actor unprivileged; name the function and the deployed code that shows it, and stop there. Read-only RPC only.

Tempo (chain 4217, tempo/v1.19.1 at a9d6748, interpreter crate evm2 at 35aa3280; source copies of earlier cycles are under the stablecoin-l1 work directories of research/network-risk/cycles/013, 015 and 018, otherwise fetch the tagged source archive) is the only one of the 21 clients whose interpreter lets a transaction start while another is running: enter_execution keeps a was_running flag. Task 1: list every non-test caller of enter_execution, transact, call_tx, the system call helpers and State::committed_copy (or their names at this revision) in the whole Tempo workspace and evm2: precompiles, the fee manager, the account keychain, T14 batch calls, payment channels, zones, the consensus and payload builder crates. Give file and line for each. Task 2: for each caller say whether the nested run can happen while a user transaction is on the call stack, and whether the nested run shares the outer transaction's transient storage map, starts with an empty one, or clears the map when it returns. Read the code that creates and clears the map (clear_transaction_state and whatever enter_execution saves and restores). Task 3: for each caller that an ordinary account can reach (by calling a precompile, by paying fees in a token, by a batch or keychain call), say whether the nested run can call the PoolManager or a token or hook that calls it, and work through three cases against the source lines above: a shared map (the nested run sees the PoolManager unlocked and the outer caller's deltas), a map cleared on return (open deltas vanish before the check at src/PoolManager.sol:112, and a sync is forgotten), and an empty map with committed writes (a payment could be counted twice). Task 4: test what can be tested with eth_call and eth_simulateV1 on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz with state overrides: a driver that unlocks the PoolManager, opens a delta, then calls each reachable precompile path and reads the lock slot and its delta with exttload before and after. Also run the test under T14 rules through a block time override of 1796745600, as cycles/018/stablecoin-l1.work/t14run.py does. Report every path where a transient slot changed or was hidden. Such a path within an ordinary account's reach is a finding with actor unprivileged; state whose money would be at risk. If every caller runs outside user transactions, say so with the lines that show it.

Public RPC nodes run an interpreter, and the public stateless validator (mega-evm, built in research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work) has reproduced the sequencer's state root on about 51,000 blocks. Read the MegaETH documentation and the node source for eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_simulateV1, the realtime API and any mega_ namespace, and establish from documentation or response fields whether any of them is served by the sequencer's executor. If one is, run the tools/opdiff/battery.py and targeted.py vectors through it. Task 3: what does the documentation or published source say about the producer's compiler? If source for it is public, read its handlers for MULMOD, SAR, SHL, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD and CALLDATALOAD for specialisations on constant operands, and check them at the five sites of the PoolManager build that cycle 17 tested on Monad (pc 22378 MULMOD by 2^128, pc 22639 MULMOD by 2^96, pc 15519 SAR, pc 16642 SHL, pc 12232 CALLDATALOAD; see OPCODES.md, cycle 17). Task 4: widen the mined evidence at exactly those sites. From the PoolManager transactions of blocks after 32,814,962 (and earlier ones not yet validated; lists are under research/network-risk/cycles/018/theme-sync-leak-census.work), pick the transactions whose traces reach each of the five program counters with operands near the edges (a 512 bit product whose high word is 1, a swap delta near the int128 bounds, a hook that returns a delta), re-run their blocks in the validator build with the pre-state anchored to the parent root, and report per site how many mined executions are now covered and whether every block's state root is reproduced. Task 5 (lead L-883): find a mined block whose state growth reached the 1,000 entry limit of F-062 and report where the transactions it skipped were placed afterwards. A mined block the validator cannot reproduce, with a PoolManager result that differs from the source at one of the sites, is a finding; say whether an ordinary account can choose the input.

Cycle 18 reran 63,540 Uniswap v3 style swaps from parent-block state with the formulas of src/libraries (research/network-risk/cycles/018/theme-hyperevm-v3-rest.work; read its notes and the verifier's remarks in cycles/018/theme-hyperevm-v3-rest.verdicts.json first). Two things remain. (a) The check is lenient: where a pool's fee moves it searches for a fee in pips that fits, and it also accepts a rerun whose price limit is set to the logged price, so only about a third of the swaps counted on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv need that branch to match. (b) About 1,010,000 swaps of the two Algebra style factories 0xf77bd082c627aa54591cf2f2eaa811fd1ab3b1f3 and 0x5f95e92c338e6453111fc55ee66d4aa1df4e8e59 were left out because their pools answer globalState() and not slot0(). Task 1, strict rerun: for the 36,665 swaps that touched the 512 bit branch, read the fee from the pool at the parent block (fee(), slot0 or globalState, or the fee a Swap or Fee event carries) and rerun with the open price limit only (no limit at the logged price unless the transaction's calldata shows that limit). Report how many still match on all five values, how many of those need the 512 bit branch (the rerun with the branch replaced by a deliberately wrong result must fail), and examine every swap that matched leniently and fails strictly. Task 2, the Algebra pools: read the pool bytecode and verified source if any (Sourcify, the HyperEVM explorers) to establish the swap step: the tick table layout, how the fee is computed (static, adaptive, a plugin call), the community fee, and the price and amount formulas. Build a collector that reads globalState(), liquidity(), the tick table and ticks at the parent block from the archive client, applies every Mint, Burn and other liquidity event of the pool earlier in the block, and reruns a seeded sample of at least 20,000 swaps. Require price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to equal the Swap log to the unit, with the fee read, not searched. Task 3: report the counts as cycle 18 did (reproduced, several steps, calls on the 512 bit branch that are needed for the match, mismatches by cause, mismatches left), save every mismatch in full, and plant the MULMOD and TickMath faults on 2,000 swaps to show the comparison can fail. A swap whose logged values differ from src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol on equal inputs, with nothing in the pool's own code to explain it, is a finding with actor unprivileged on chain 999. Use https://rpc.purroofgroup.com for parent state (the official endpoint ignores historical block tags in eth_call) and https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm for logs; read-only eth_call, eth_getLogs and eth_getStorageAt only.
